manifest.name: dsh-preset-switch
manifest.description: Switch agent presets in any DSH conversation — even ones that already have messages.

readme.text: A small plugin that lets you **switch the Agent Preset mid-conversation** in DeepSeek Harness — even in conversations that already have messages.

By default, DSH only lets you pick a Preset in an **empty conversation**; once a conversation has messages, the Preset gets locked and can't be changed.

This plugin adds a dropdown to the conversation header so you can switch to another Preset (a different set of tools + prompt configuration) while a conversation is in progress — without opening a new one and losing context.

1. Install the plugin (see "Install" below).
2. Open any conversation.
3. Click the Preset dropdown in the header and pick a target Preset.
4. Empty conversations switch immediately; **conversations that already have messages ask for confirmation first** (to avoid accidental switches).

- **Only works in the currently open conversation.** A historical conversation that isn't open in the UI must be opened first before you can switch it.
- After switching, **new turns** continue with the new Preset's tools and prompt.
Switching a Preset means swapping one set of "tools + prompt" for another. So when you switch **mid-conversation**, keep these in mind:

- **Past tool calls may no longer line up**: tools used earlier may not exist in the new Preset. The model may see tool calls in the history that it no longer recognizes, which can confuse it or cause it to repeat calls.
- **Behavior may "jump"**: with a different prompt, the model's tone, role, and capability boundaries change, so conversational continuity can suffer.
- **Results aren't guaranteed to be better**: switching to a Preset that doesn't fit the current task can naturally make replies worse — that's not a broken install, just a mismatched Preset.

In short:

> **No switching, no impact.** This plugin only acts when you actively choose to switch; mid-conversation switching is a double-edged sword — helpful when used well, worse when used poorly.
